info.title: Name That LLM Open Pool: 224k Clean Passages
info.subtitle: Generation settings, fidelity audit, verified Gemini 3.7, recovered prompts
info.description:
# Name That LLM Open Pool v14: 223,840 clean passages, ready to train

**v14 adds 11,501 passages, removes 284 mislabelled ones, and records how every passage was generated.**
- **How each passage was generated (new columns):** `gen_reasoning` (the reasoning setting, known for 54% of rows), `gen_route`, `gen_served_model`, `gen_date`
  and `flag_kb_proxy_after_ruling`, plus `source_protocol.csv`, the generation protocol each of the 61 sources declares, with the file it was read from.
- **Which passages look like the real ones (new files):** a classifier trained only on the competition's train.csv scores every source and label against
  real passages (`fidelity_by_label.csv`, `fidelity_by_source.csv`, `fidelity_by_reasoning.csv`). The main finding is below: **`kimi-k3` written with reasoning
  switched off does not look like the real `kimi-k3`.**
- **Mislabelled rows removed:** 284 passages of one source were written by models outside the 18 labels (the source's own model column shows it), see Corrections.
- **New passages:** darragh1walsh 5,158, adurey 4,152, parkjinsu1 2,088, toanplam 103, all from the Kaggle Benchmarks proxy and the 12 labels it serves.

`gemini-3.7-flash` keeps only rows from a documented Vertex AI route, because other APIs have served 3.8 under that name since 2026-10-08.
Passages carry a recovered prompt id wherever one could be established (99.7% of rows), and the `match_weight` column samples passages whose typography matches the real ones.
Every passage in the main file passed all quality, genre and licence checks, so you can train on the whole file with no filtering.
The one subset worth testing first is `kimi-k3` generated with reasoning on (finding 1 below).

> **Please support this dataset with an upvote** if it helps you. Building and testing it took a lot of GPU time and
> effort, and votes help every competitor find the same free, clean data. If you think something here is wrong,
> please say so in the comments.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Passages | **223,840**, all 18 competition labels |
| Left out of the main file | 89,037 rows (see below; ids in `removed_rows.csv`) |
| Words per passage | median 102, range 36-275 |
| Source datasets | 61, all CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 or CC0; how each generated is in `source_protocol.csv` |
| Recovered prompts | 17,671 with prompt text; 711 answered by all 18 labels |
| Generation setting known | 54% of rows (`gen_reasoning`) |
| Contains competition data? | **No.** No train copies, nothing close to train content, no answers to train prompts. |
| License | **CC BY-SA 4.0** |

## New in v14: which passages look like the real ones

**Method.** A TF-IDF + logistic regression classifier is trained only on the 2,699 real train passages. Scored on train prompts it never saw (5 folds grouped by prompt),
it names the right label for 33% of real passages (labels weighted equally). The same classifier then scores every pool passage. If a source's passages
of a label are recognised much less often than real passages of that label, they differ from the real ones in some way the classifier can see. It is a weak classifier,
so read it for large groups, never to filter single passages. `fidelity_ratio` = pool recognition rate / real recognition rate (1 means "as recognisable as real").

**Finding 1: the reasoning setting decides whether `kimi-k3` looks real.** Real `kimi-k3` passages are recognised 31% of the time. In the pool:

| `kimi-k3` passages by `gen_reasoning` | Passages | Recognised as `kimi-k3` |
|---|---|---|
| high | 2,673 | 25% |
| default | 2,871 | 11% |
| unknown | 2,054 | 11% |
| off | 1,702 | 8% |
| other | 374 | 7% |
| low | 57 | 4% |

The same holds inside one source with the same prompts and filters (willrice): reasoning high 21%, reasoning off 8%.
So the real `kimi-k3` passages were most likely written with reasoning on. If you train on pool `kimi-k3`, try `pool[(pool.model == "kimi-k3") & (pool.gen_reasoning == "high")]` first.
The same direction shows for `glm-5.3` and `qwen3.8-max` at reasoning low, on fewer passages (`fidelity_by_reasoning.csv`). For the GPT, Gemini and Claude labels the differences
between settings are smaller and point in no consistent direction (and each setting there mixes different sources).
This was also found by others: a label audit credited to samarth1006 drops `kimi-k3` sources that a train-only model rarely recognises.

**Finding 2: `glm-5.3` does not need reprocessing.** Real `glm-5.3` already reads like Claude to a classifier (thread 755314): it puts 40% of its probability on the
Claude labels. Pool `glm-5.3` does the same (42%), and its sources agree with each other, so the Claude-like style is the model's own, not a labelling error.

**Finding 3: the widest gaps are `kimi-k3` (46%), `qwen3.8-max` (51%), `claude-opus-4-8` (54%)** (pool recognition as a share of the real rate).
The GPT labels range from 79% to 102%. For `claude-opus-4-8` the gap comes mostly from a few large sources,
see `fidelity_by_source.csv`, which lists every source and label with 30 or more passages.

## Why clean: the evidence

**1. The raw pool did not look like real passages.** Style rates in the competition's train.csv against the raw pool
(v7) and v9, with each label weighted equally:

| Feature | Real train | Raw pool v7 | v9 clean |
|---|---|---|---|
| ends with . ! ? or quote | 99.9% | 93.4% | 99.4% |
| uses we / our / us | 30.7% | 15.5% | 15.5% |
| uses I / me / my | 6.4% | 15.4% | 5.8% |
| contains a digit | 9.9% | 29.2% | 20.8% |
| contains ( ) | 1.1% | 11.4% | 4.1% |
| contains / | 0.3% | 11.6% | 1.6% |
| contains straight " | 4.0% | 19.1% | 8.7% |
| contains a colon | 52.1% | 54.0% | 46.6% |
| API dump or refusal | 0.0% | 8.2% | 0.0% |

The "we / our / us" gap does not move with cleaning. It comes from the host's prompts, not from junk.

**2. At equal size, clean data trains a better model.** A Qwen3-1.7B LoRA classifier was trained only on pool data,
with exactly 2,500 passages per label (45,000 in total) in every run. It was then scored on all 2,699 competition
train passages, whose prompts it never saw. Mean of 2 seeds:

| Training data (45k passages) | Balanced acc. | vs raw v1-5 |
|---|---|---|
| raw pool v1-5 | 0.466 | +0.000 |
| raw pool v1-7 | 0.464 | -0.001 |
| v1-5 minus hard junk | 0.474 | +0.009 |
| v1-5 minus junk and off-genre sources | 0.493 | +0.027 |
| v1-7 minus junk and off-genre sources | 0.492 | +0.026 |

**3. The dirtiest labels gain the most.** Across the 18 labels, the share of junk and off-genre text in a label's raw
sample correlates with its recall gain after cleaning (Spearman 0.64). kimi-k3 gained +16 recall points and
claude-opus-4-8 +13.

**4. Stricter filters were tested too** (same setup):

| Training data (45k passages) | Balanced acc. | vs clean v1-7, same seed | Seeds |
|---|---|---|---|
| v1-7 minus junk and off-genre sources | 0.492 | +0.000 | 2 |
| the same plus licence/provenance filters and 8.6k new passages | 0.492 | +0.000 | 2 |
| the previous row minus Kaggle Benchmarks proxy rows | 0.491 | -0.001 | 2 |
| the previous-but-one row minus the 30% least train-like passages per label | 0.488 | -0.004 | 2 |

v9 and v10 use the licence and provenance filters (no loss) and keep the Kaggle Benchmarks proxy rows, flagged in
`flag_kb_proxy`. Selecting only the most train-like passages did not help, so they do not filter on `style_score`.
All runs are in `dataq_results.csv`.

**5. Full-size check on the leaderboard.** The same DeBERTa-v3-large recipe was trained twice, changing only the pool:
raw v7 (254k passages) scored **0.585** public LB, clean v9 (193k passages) scored **0.587**. A quarter fewer passages,
same or slightly better score. Internal pool-based validation said v9 was worse, so do not judge data changes by it.

**6. Tests behind v11: four more tests** (same setup, 2 seeds per training set, compared at the same seed with v10 minus the source that is no longer public). Each cell is the change in balanced
accuracy, with a 95% interval from resampling prompts. The interval does not include training randomness, so the two single-seed results are shown too.

| Change tested alone | All 150 train prompts | Half of prompts not used to fit it | Seed 0 / seed 1 | 2 answers per prompt | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gemini-3.7 from Vertex AI sources only | +0.009 (+0.000 to +0.019) | +0.020 (+0.007 to +0.033) | +0.007 / +0.006 | +0.009 (-0.016 to +0.034) | **Adopted**: the main file now keeps only documented Vertex AI rows for this label |
| Sampling matched to real typography and length | +0.026 (+0.012 to +0.039) | +0.027 (+0.006 to +0.047) | +0.013 / +0.022 | +0.012 (-0.021 to +0.045) | **Added** as the optional `match_weight` column |
| Prompts with the most labels first | +0.009 (-0.005 to +0.022) | +0.024 (+0.002 to +0.044) | +0.016 / -0.003 | -0.006 (-0.036 to +0.027) | Not proven. `panel_labels` lets you try it |
| Adding prvsiyan extended rows | -0.009 (-0.023 to +0.004) | +0.013 (-0.005 to +0.032) | -0.001 / -0.005 | -0.004 (-0.035 to +0.026) | Not added (see correction below) |

- **Why the Gemini change:** within one large source, 3.7 and 3.8 rows could not be told apart (AUC 0.498), while 3.6 and 3.8 could (0.776).
  With Vertex-only rows, recall on real passages moved: 3.7 from 0.21 to 0.42, 3.8 from 0.59 to 0.64,
  and 3.6 fell from 0.63 to 0.47. The net effect is positive but this is not a free win for every label.
- **Why the typography weights:** on average a marker's rate sits 6.4 points from the real rate, and about 0 after weighting (by construction: the weights are fitted to these markers). Word hyphens on the
  Gemini labels: real 12%, pool 44%, weighted 12%. The test fitted its targets on one half of the train prompts and scored the other half.
  The column in this file uses all train prompts, so a validation on train.csv after using it will read slightly high.
- **Metric note:** the earlier prompt-centred score is not used for these decisions. With 17-18 answers per prompt it over-predicts some labels
  (baseline: 466 predictions of gemini-3.1 at 0.32 precision, none of kimi-k3). The "2 answers per prompt" column draws two passages per prompt and centres within the pair.
  Its intervals include zero: on that cut the Gemini and typography changes point the right way, but the test is not large enough to prove them alone.
- **Not tested as a whole:** each change was measured alone, and the passages added in v11 (10,294), v12 (20,781), v13 (1,254) and v14 (11,501) were not part of these tests. All runs are in `dataq4_runs.csv` and `dataq4_paired.csv`.

## What is left out of the main file

| Reason (first matching) | Rows |
|---|---|
| Off-genre sources (chat logs, benchmark answers, reasoning traces) | 30,992 |
| Raw API responses stored as text (HTTP headers, JSON) | 13,114 |
| gemini-3.7-flash without a documented Vertex AI route: moved to `gemini37_unverified.parquet`, not deleted | 10,838 |
| Source dataset no longer public | 9,815 |
| prvsiyan extended rows: on-genre and well documented, tested in v11 with no gain (correction below) | 7,492 |
| Refusals | 6,939 |
| Licence or provenance risk (licence-excluded source re-uploaded as CC0, unverifiable origin) | 4,289 |
| Chat preambles, CJK text, length outside 36-275 words, same text with two labels | 2,197 |
| Cut off mid-sentence | 1,515 |
| Typography the label never uses in train (e.g. em dash for some Gemini labels) | 1,278 |
| Answers to the competition's train prompts | 284 |
| Written by a model that is not one of the 18 labels, per the source's own model column (v14) | 284 |

## Columns of `ntl_open_pool.parquet`

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | stable row id, unchanged since v1 |
| `text` | the passage |
| `model` | label as published by the source (one of the 18 competition labels) |
| `lab` | provider: anthropic, google, openai, zai, moonshot, qwen |
| `prompt_group` | source and the source's own prompt id. Unreliable across sources: use `prompt_canon` |
| `source_dataset` | Kaggle dataset credited for this passage |
| `source_file` | file inside that dataset |
| `source_license` | licence of `source_dataset` |
| `origin_hint` | the source's own src/source column, if it had one |
| `n_words` | whitespace word count |
| `also_in` | every source dataset containing this exact passage, separated by semicolons |
| `n_sources` | number of datasets in `also_in` |
| `max_cos_train` | highest TF-IDF cosine to any competition train passage (all below 0.3) |
| `max_sim_train_prompt` | highest TF-IDF cosine to any competition train prompt centroid |
| `style_score` | probability that a style-only model (punctuation, pronouns, rhythm, function words; no topic words) takes the passage for a real train passage |
| `flag_kb_proxy` | generated through the Kaggle Benchmarks proxy (84,685 rows). Allowed as public community data; drop with `df[~df.flag_kb_proxy]` to be strict |
| `flag_gemini37_routing_risk` | always False in the main file since v11; the 3.7 rows at risk are in `gemini37_unverified.parquet` |
| `flag_near_train_prompt`, `flag_train_prompt_regen` | always False since v9 (those rows were removed); kept so code written for older versions still runs |
| `prompt_canon` | recovered prompt id, shared across sources when it starts with `p`. Starts with `s` when known only inside one source; empty when unknown. Use it for group splits |
| `panel_labels` | number of labels that answered this prompt in this file (1-18) |
| `prompt_evidence` | how the prompt was found: `own_text` 65,109, `own_bank` 75,924, `other_text` 27,191, `centroid` 14,169 (matched by content; at most about 3% false matches in the hold-out tests run for v11-v14), `id_only` 40,775, `none` 672 |
| `match_weight` | sampling weight within a label, mean 1, so that typography and length match real passages. Use for sampling, not as a loss weight unless you test it |
| `gen_reasoning` | reasoning setting the passage was generated with: default, off, minimal, low, medium, high, other or unknown (unknown 101,876, default 89,650, low 21,878, high 3,412, other 2,823, off 2,241, minimal 1,235, medium 725) |
| `gen_reasoning_evidence` | where `gen_reasoning` comes from: `row` = the source file's own column (103,889), `source_docs` = the source states one setting for all its rows (18,075), `unknown` |
| `gen_reasoning_raw` | the source's own value, as written (e.g. `effort=minimal`, `think_low`) |
| `gen_route` | route or provider in the source file (e.g. `kaggle_proxy`, `vertex`, `Moonshot AI`); empty when not recorded |
| `gen_served_model` | model id the API returned, when the source recorded it |
| `gen_date` | generation date (UTC) in the source file, or from its batch name; empty when not recorded |
| `flag_kb_proxy_after_ruling` | Kaggle Benchmarks proxy row generated after the hosts said the proxy quota is not meant for building training data (thread 752084, 2026-10-28) (17,876 rows, 7 sources). The hosts also said public datasets made this way are fine to train on. A lower bound: sources that record no date are not flagged |

## Quickstart

```python
import pandas as pd
pool = pd.read_parquet("/kaggle/input/name-that-llm-open-pool/ntl_open_pool.parquet")
print(len(pool), pool.model.value_counts())   # train on all of it

# or a fixed number per label, matched to real typography
sample = pool.groupby("model", group_keys=False).apply(
    lambda d: d.sample(min(2500, len(d)), weights="match_weight", random_state=0))
```

## Caveats

- **Labels are the publishers' claims.** Nothing here re-verifies which model produced a passage. The Gemini 3.7 route comes from each source's own documentation.
- **The kilupy Claude passages (added in v12) answer synthetic prompts** (domain x subject x framing), not host-style ones, and their typography differs from the real passages:
  em dash in 55% of their `claude-fable-5` rows against 83% in train, and 52% against 81% for `claude-opus-5`.
  `match_weight` brings each label's rate back to the real one, but the effective sample of the Claude labels is 62% of their rows, against 73% in v11.
  The Claude labels now hold a larger share of the file, so balance classes when you sample.
- **Every v13 and v14 passage came through the Kaggle Benchmarks proxy** (`flag_kb_proxy` is True), and 17,876 proxy rows in the file were generated after the hosts' 2026-10-28 answer on the proxy quota
  (`flag_kb_proxy_after_ruling`). The hosts allow training on public datasets made this way; drop either flag if you want to be strict.
- **`gen_reasoning` is unknown for 46% of rows**, mostly sources that did not record it. The fidelity tables use a weak classifier: read them for large groups only.
- **`gemini-3.7-flash` is now the smallest label** (3,541 passages from 5 sources), so its source mix is narrower.
- **Heavy typography weighting shrinks the usable sample:** the effective share of a label's rows under `match_weight` ranges from 31% to 68%.
- **The tests use a 1.7B model at a fixed 45k passages.** Larger models are more robust to noise, so the gain at full
  scale may be smaller. A full-size result will be posted in the discussion thread.
- **Not the hosts' prompts.** Cross-validation that mixes pool data into training reads a few points higher than the LB.
- **Uneven classes** (about 4k for `gemini-3.7-flash` up to about
  23k for `gemini-3.8-flash`). Use class weights or sampling.

## Corrections

- **prvsiyan's extended dataset is not off-genre.** v9 wrongly placed it in the off-genre row. It is on-genre and has some of the best provenance in this
  competition, including a served-model check on every call. Tested alone, adding its rows gave no gain, so they stay out, except its 266 Vertex AI
  `gemini-3.7-flash` rows, which are back in the main file (old ids kept where they had one). That no-gain result is about one small test, not about the author's work.
- **`flag_kb_proxy` was set per source, which marked 5,501 non-proxy rows as proxy.** Fixed from each source's own route column: alperen5252525 Vertex AI Gemini 2,573, arxitekton OpenRouter 2,846, earthmaker OpenRouter 82. Sources without a route column keep the flag they had, so treat it as an upper bound.
- **284 passages had the wrong label (removed in v14).** In illiadolenko/ntl-generated-corpus-v1, the source's own `source_slug` column shows these were written by models that are not
  competition labels: 121 labelled `gemini-3.6-flash`, 101 labelled `gpt-5.6-luna`, 43 labelled `claude-opus-4-8`, 19 labelled `claude-fable-5` (by gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gpt-6-luna, claude-opus-4-7 and claude-haiku-5-5). They are listed in `removed_rows.csv`
  as `served_model_not_the_label`. A check of every model-id column in every source file found no other case.
- **The v10 changelog said one source had no documentation.** It has a short description; what it does not state is the generation route.

  `fidelity_by_label.csv`, `fidelity_by_source.csv`, `fidelity_by_reasoning.csv`. Author-quarantined rows (Gemini text with em dashes replaced by commas) were not taken.
